name: Baradin Bay
summary: In Baradin Bay, reefs and wrecks make each crossing perilous. Its waters lie between Khaz Modan, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, and southern Lordaeron. Kul Tiras once patrolled the bay with a powerful navy during the Second War.

sections.title: A Strategic Waterway
sections.body: Baradin Bay links the harbors of the Eastern Kingdoms. Menethil Harbor lies on its Wetlands shore, and Southshore stands in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Shallow sandbanks and jagged shoals threaten ships, as do murlocs, crocolisks, and deep-sea sharks.

sections.title: Graveyard of the Fleets
sections.body: During the Second War, Kul Tiras and the Horde fought across Baradin Bay. The broken hulls of the Kul Tiran Third Fleet, called the Lost Fleet, lie half-submerged along the Wetlands coast. Other ships sank at Drowned Reef. Hostile spirits, salvagers, and sea beasts haunt the waters around the ruined ships.

faq.q: What major ports are located along Baradin Bay?
faq.answer: Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands and Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills are the bay's chief ports, sustaining naval travel across the sea.

faq.q: Why are there so many shipwrecks along the bay's coast?
faq.answer: The wrecks along the Wetlands shore belong to the Lost Fleet, the Kul Tiras Third Fleet destroyed during the Second War. Other ships sank on Drowned Reef off the Arathi coast.

faq.q: What threats can be found in the waters of Baradin Bay?
aliases: is it safe to swim in baradin bay
faq.answer: Murlocs and swamp crocolisks threaten the shallows. Deeper waters hold predatory crabs, sharks, and restless spirits of drowned sailors.
Baradin Bay borders northwestern Dun Morogh, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, southern Hillsbrad, and Gilneas.

angles.text: For the Alliance, Baradin Bay links operations in Khaz Modan with outposts in Arathi and Hillsbrad. Naval hazards and wreckage make every crossing risky.
For humans, especially those tracing their lineage to Kul Tiras or Lordaeron, Baradin Bay is solemn ground where Second War sailors rest beneath the waves.
